title: Cellular Network Traffic Scheduling With Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: Sandeep Chinchali; Pan Hu; Tianshu Chu; Manu Sharma; Manu Bansal; Rakesh Misra; Marco Pavone; Sachin Katti
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
architecture: Centralised controller scheduling delay-tolerant traffic of IoT devices alongside real-time traffic in a cellular network
problem: Scheduling delay-tolerant software updates and data backups of IoT devices in cellular networks without violating strict service guarantees of real-time applications (voice, video).
input_parameters: Per-device queue/backlog state and channel state; per-application delay tolerance (deadline is a constant per application, not a constraint).
decision_variables: Which device to schedule in each time slot, and at what rate.
objective: Minimise time-averaged queue backlog (delay) of delay-tolerant traffic while respecting real-time service guarantees, formulated as a Lyapunov-drift-plus-penalty problem.
constraints: Real-time applications must receive fixed minimum rates; stability of delay-tolerant queues.
algorithm: Deep reinforcement learning with a policy-gradient / actor-critic style parameterisation of the scheduling policy, trained to approximate the solution of a per-slot optimisation derived from Lyapunov drift-plus-penalty.
optimization_method: Lyapunov stochastic optimisation combined with DRL function approximation
simulator: Custom simulation; an RF throughput model (11.4% median error, 890 Kbps RMSE) and an LSTM forecast (14.8% median error) are used as inputs
traffic_model: Delay-tolerant background traffic (software updates, backup) plus constant-rate real-time flows
network_scale: NA (paper studies a single base station serving many IoT devices; exact counts not verified from the retrieved record)
baselines: Heuristic scheduler; stochastic MPC; offline dynamic-programming oracle
metrics: IoT traffic served; median gain; fraction of oracle performance
main_results: Median IoT-traffic gain 14.7% under the alpha=2 policy; the learned scheduler serves 2.06x as much IoT traffic as the heuristic; RL reaches ~80% of the offline dynamic-programming oracle versus ~62% for stochastic MPC. Spectrum-cost saving of $661M is an extrapolation, not a measurement.
limitations: Single-cell simulation; learned component approximates a Lyapunov-derived policy; no 5G core/slicing; the headline dollar figure is an extrapolation.
reproducibility_notes: No public artifact identified from the sources retrieved in this session.

authors: Karim Boutiba; Adlen Ksentini; Bouziane Brik; Yacine Challal; Amar Balla

problem: Dynamically assign bandwidth parts and numerologies to running 5G NR slices such that each slice's QoS requirement (URLLC latency, eMBB throughput) is met while minimising PRBs consumed.

objective: Enforce slice QoS (uRLLC deadline, eMBB throughput) while minimising PRBs allocated to eMBB slices
constraints: uRLLC maximum latency, eMBB desired throughput, NR numerology/BWP limits

limitations: Accepted-manuscript version read rather than the typeset version; RAN-only scope (core and transport explicitly out of scope); control law is a simple additive rule rather than an optimiser, and no learning is used.
